events.content:
I want a small Next.js app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

message.content:
I want a small Next.js app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

events.content:
The app is built. I ran the production build and went through each thing you asked for against a live server.

**Run it:** `npm run dev`, or `npm run build && npm start`, then open http://localhost:3000.

**What it does**
- **Home page** shows "Currently reading", then "Finished" (most recently finished first), then a form to add a book with title, author and notes.
- **Mark finished** is a button on each book you're reading, on the home page and on the book's own page. It also records the date.
- **Book page** (`/books/<id>`) shows the title, author, whether you're reading or finished it, and your notes. Every book gets its own permanent URL, so that's the link you send someone. There's a "Copy link" button, and a link to a book that doesn't exist shows a "Book not found" page.
- **Saving:** books go to `data/books.json`, created on your first add. You can point it at another file with `BOOKS_FILE=/path/to/books.json`.

**Checked**
- Added two books through the form, marked one finished, and it moved to the "Finished" list with the right date.
- After restarting the server, both books were still there.
- HTML typed into the notes shows up as plain text and doesn't run.
- The build and typecheck pass, and 7 tests on the saving code pass (`npm test`). The tests cover two cases that could lose books: saving several at once, and a damaged file. If `books.json` becomes unreadable, the app shows an error and leaves the file alone rather than replacing your books with an empty list.

**Things to know**
- **Sharing only works if the other person can reach the app.** On localhost, a link you send won't open for anyone else. The app would have to be hosted somewhere, on a server with a persistent disk so the JSON file isn't wiped. There are no accounts, so anyone who can reach it can also add books and mark them finished.
- **Notes can't be edited yet.** You write them when you add a book. Editing them later would be a small addition if you want it.

content.text:
The app is built. I ran the production build and went through each thing you asked for against a live server.

**Run it:** `npm run dev`, or `npm run build && npm start`, then open http://localhost:3000.

**What it does**
- **Home page** shows "Currently reading", then "Finished" (most recently finished first), then a form to add a book with title, author and notes.
- **Mark finished** is a button on each book you're reading, on the home page and on the book's own page. It also records the date.
- **Book page** (`/books/<id>`) shows the title, author, whether you're reading or finished it, and your notes. Every book gets its own permanent URL, so that's the link you send someone. There's a "Copy link" button, and a link to a book that doesn't exist shows a "Book not found" page.
- **Saving:** books go to `data/books.json`, created on your first add. You can point it at another file with `BOOKS_FILE=/path/to/books.json`.

**Checked**
- Added two books through the form, marked one finished, and it moved to the "Finished" list with the right date.
- After restarting the server, both books were still there.
- HTML typed into the notes shows up as plain text and doesn't run.
- The build and typecheck pass, and 7 tests on the saving code pass (`npm test`). The tests cover two cases that could lose books: saving several at once, and a damaged file. If `books.json` becomes unreadable, the app shows an error and leaves the file alone rather than replacing your books with an empty list.

**Things to know**
- **Sharing only works if the other person can reach the app.** On localhost, a link you send won't open for anyone else. The app would have to be hosted somewhere, on a server with a persistent disk so the JSON file isn't wiped. There are no accounts, so anyone who can reach it can also add books and mark them finished.
- **Notes can't be edited yet.** You write them when you add a book. Editing them later would be a small addition if you want it.
- **Your book list isn't committed to git.** `data/` is in `.gitignore`; remove that line if you do want it in the repo.
- `npm audit` reports a moderate warning in the test tool (vitest) that was already in the project. It only affects tests, not the app, and fixing it means a major vitest upgrade, so I left it.

I haven't committed anything.
